broader_coverage.reasoning: General lower bounds in an unrestricted class do not determine this restricted exact minimum; last-sign-radius theorems do not imply a length optimum when the negative set can be separated from zero.

evidence: The motivating problem is an infimum over general Fourier eigenfunctions, not a computation on {0,4,8} Hermite modes.
Known last-sign-radius inequalities only constrain outermost negative root; they allow many different negative-set lengths.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither a coarse global measure bound nor knowledge of the last zero implies the exact optimum with its detached symmetric interval. The new theorem is narrower in function class and finer in its objective and equality case.

value.rationale: The source explicitly motivates negative-set measure as an uncertainty invariant. The first nontrivial three-mode Fourier +1 cutoff has a strict radical optimum and unique optimizer, with its negative set disconnected from the origin. This provides a nontrivial, reproducible benchmark beyond routine Gaussian sign-radius estimates.
